## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/02.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">Student Growth Percentiles
References

Student Growth Percentiles

Student Growth Percentiles are a norm referenced growth
metric capable of being embedded within criterion referenced
assessment/accountability systems.
Student Growth Percentiles were developed by Dr. Damian
Betebenner at The Center for Assessment to help states use
their longitudinal assessment data to understand the progress
of students and its relationship to education quality.
Student Growth Percentiles have been adopted for use by four
states: Colorado, Massachusetts, Indiana, and Arizona and
are being piloted in many other states including Rhode Island
and New Hampshire.
The method formed the basis of the Colorado Department of
Education’s successful application to USED under the Growth
Model Pilot Program for use as part of AYP.

D. W. Betebenner Student Growth Percentiles</div>
```

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/03.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">Student Growth Percentiles
References

What are the relevant questions?

Growth models address specific questions
Different growth analysis techniques are good at
answering different questions.
It is critical to understand these different questions.
Different questions lead to different conversations which
lead to different uses and outcomes.

Questions form the vocabulary of later conversations
Starting with the right questions simplifies development
and motivating the proper use of the growth model results.
It’s all about the conversations you want to have. The
questions set the table for those conversations.

D. W. Betebenner Student Growth Percentiles</div>
```

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/04.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">Student Growth Percentiles
References

What are the relevant questions for parents?

Yen (2007), from a state survey of parents, teachers and
administrators, compiled a list of frequently voiced
questions/concerns by stakeholder group.

Parent Questions
Did my child make a year’s worth of progress in a year?
Is my child growing appropriately toward meeting state
standards?
Is my child growing as much in Math as Reading?
Did my child grow as much this year as last year?

D. W. Betebenner Student Growth Percentiles</div>
```

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/05.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">Student Growth Percentiles
References

What are the relevant questions for teachers?

Yen (2007), from a state survey of parents, teachers and
administrators, compiled a list of frequently voiced
questions/concerns by stakeholder group.

Teacher Questions
Did my students make a year’s worth of progress in a
year?
Did my students grow appropriately toward meeting state
standards?
How close are my students to becoming Proficient?
Are there students with unusually low growth who need
special attention?

D. W. Betebenner Student Growth Percentiles</div>
```

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/06.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">Student Growth Percentiles
References

What are the relevant questions for administrators?
Yen (2007), from a state survey of parents, teachers and
administrators, compiled a list of frequently voiced
questions/concerns by stakeholder group.

Administrator Questions
Did the students in our district/school make a year’s worth
of progress in all content areas?
Are our students growing appropriately toward meeting
state standards?
Does this school/program show as much growth as that
one?
Can I measure student growth even for students who do
not change proficiency categories?
Can I pool together results from different grades to draw
summary conclusions?
D. W. Betebenner Student Growth Percentiles</div>
```

## {.archive-slide background-image="slides/07.webp" background-size="contain" background-color="#14140f"}

```{=html}
<div class="archive-text">Student Growth Percentiles
References

Student Growth Percentiles

Student growth percentiles allows stakeholders to answer all
of the questions just mentioned.
A common metric usable by diverse stakeholders (e.g.,
parents, teachers, principals, administrators, and policy
makers) creates the possibility for transformative change.

D. W. Betebenner Student Growth Percentiles</div>
```
